title: InfoQ Launches High-Performing Teams Certification Program
gist: InfoQ opened enrollment for a five-week, $1,470 live online High-Performing Teams certification cohort (Nov 17 to Dec 17, 2026) led by Olimpiu Pop. The syllabus centers on how team design, flow, ownership, AI agents in delivery and metrics interact, signalling that AI-shifted delivery bottlenecks are now a core engineering-management training topic.

insights.claim: InfoQ's first High-Performing Teams certification cohort runs online from November 17 to December 17, 2026, with two two-hour sessions per week, and costs $1,470.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Tech media brands are monetizing via paid cohort-based certifications, a revenue line beyond advertising.
insights.locator: InfoQ has opened enrollment for the first cohort

insights.claim: The InfoQ program targets small cohorts of senior engineers and architects, uses selected QCon talks as weekly starting material, keeps sessions unrecorded for confidentiality, and awards certification on attendance, participation and a group capstone.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Reuses existing conference content as courseware, a low-marginal-cost education model.
insights.locator: The program is conducted with a small cohort

insights.claim: A dedicated week of the InfoQ curriculum covers introducing AI agents into software delivery: which work can be delegated, where human judgment remains necessary, and what extra controls or artifacts are required.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Delegation boundaries and controls for AI agents are now mainstream engineering-management concerns, supporting demand for agent governance tooling.
insights.locator: The third week examines the introduction of AI agents

insights.claim: The curriculum treats AI as shifting delivery bottlenecks, requiring re-evaluation of engineering metrics and which measures remain useful as output increases.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Output-based productivity metrics lose meaning under AI-assisted coding; watch vendors of engineering-intelligence and measurement platforms.

insights.claim: The final week covers responsible AI, including the ethical and environmental implications of AI-enabled delivery, folded into each group's team operating model.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Environmental cost of AI is entering engineering-leadership curricula.
insights.locator: The final week addresses responsible AI
